Title:
New composer install behind proxy

Description:
Recently I notice the way composer install change and it doesn't work for me now. When I try: ``` php -r "readfile('https://getcomposer.org/installer');" > composer-setup.php PHP Warning: readfile(): php_network_getaddresses: getaddrinfo failed: Name or service not known in Command line code on line 1 PHP Warning: readfile(https://getcomposer.org/installer): failed to open stream: php_network_getaddresses: getaddrinfo failed: Name or service not known in Command line code on line 1 ``` However as a workaround I create the following script: ``` $auth = base64_encode('USER:PASSWORD'); $aContext = array( 'http' => array( 'proxy' => 'tcp://PROXY:PORT', 'request_fulluri' => true, 'header' => "Proxy-Authorization: Basic $auth", ), ); $cxContext = stream_context_create($aContext); file_get_contents("http://getcomposer.org/installer", False, $cxContext); ``` So when I run It `php -f test.php > composer-setup.php` I am able to pull It down. ``` php -r "echo hash('SHA384', file_get_contents('composer-setup.php'));" 781c98992e23d4a5ce559daf0170f8a9b3b91331ddc4a3fa9f7d42b6d981513cdc1411730112495fbf9d59cffbf20fb2 ``` But when I try to run the setup: ``` All settings correct for using Composer Downloading... Download failed: file_get_contents(https://getcomposer.org/composer.phar.sig): failed to open stream: Cannot connect to HTTPS server through proxy Download failed: file_get_contents(https://getcomposer.org/composer.phar.sig): failed to open stream: Cannot connect to HTTPS server through proxy file_get_contents(https://getcomposer.org/composer.phar): failed to open stream: Cannot connect to HTTPS server through proxy Downloading... - AFAIR it uses https for packages.json to make sure noone in the middle can intercept the process and let you download malicous packages. the packages itself are downloaded via http for perf reasons.
- Hmm that's right, that's really a micro-optimization. The consequence however seems the same - `400 Bad Request` nearly always boils down to speaking SSL to an unencrypted HTTP server in my experience.
- It's not really a micro optimization, the https connection setup time is quite long and since php streams can't do keepalive we end up opening many connections.
- If you pass in a `https://` URL it will use the value from `http_proxy` according to that line. Good point about the protocol switching, if you get a redirect to a URL that uses a different proxy or should bypass a proxy it will still attempt to use the proxy.
- Yes it does but line 49 below overwrites it with the `HTTPS_PROXY` value if set and https url. The underlying issue seems to be indeed that protocol switches do not use the right URL. Bringing us to that the optimization, micro or not, is invalid as http://packagist.org/p/provider-2013%24907f12bc7ed756034fb97405ced3ebfe769ac49a0786554246a14a1b23ffba8e.json instantly redirects with a 307 to the https version right now. So yes, it would appear that the issue is with Composer still trying those URLs as plain http, not setting the `HTTPS_PROXY` for that, and the internal redirect being handled at curl level causing the `http_proxy` to be used for https, explaining the 400 error.
- There is no redirect to https for static files. This one redirects because it's a 404 so it gets handled by symfony which then redirects to force https. If you try a valid url it'll go through over http just fine.
- Errr true, but why is that URL invalid as I copy/pasted it from the error logs? ``` [Composer\Downloader\TransportException] The 'http://packagist.org/p/provider-2013%24907f12bc7ed756034fb97405ced3ebfe769ac49a0786554246a14a1b23ffba8e.json' URL could not be accessed: HTTP/1.0 400 Bad Request ```
- Because those URLs are based on the file content hash so they change often and old files get cleaned up.
- That fast? So it could very well be that the proxy is caching the `packages.json` a day as it's a static file, serving the client a somewhat outdated version, referencing a sub-include that no longer exists, causing the HTTPS redirect, thus exposing the HTTPS_PROXY mismatch issue on curl internal redirects?
- If the proxy is completely borked and caching what it shouldn't cache, sure it's possible. We clean up files hourly IIRC.
- The response headers on `packages.json` are: ``` Accept-Ranges:bytes Connection:keep-alive Content-Length:1181 Content-Type:application/json Date:Fri, 19 Feb 2016 15:00:38 GMT ETag:"56c72e01-49d" Last-Modified:Fri, 19 Feb 2016 15:00:17 GMT Server:nginx ``` Just an ETag, no `Cache-control` or `Expires`. I wouldn't at all be surprised if this is what's happening if the file starts causing this after an hour. As there is no `must-revalidate` rule or anything these headers tell the proxy it's essentially fine to cache this file for an arbitrary time. I would at the very least configure nginx to add: cache-control: private, max-age=0, no-cache,
- Fair enough, I added no-cache headers on that file now.
- And if `HTTP_PROXY` is unset? Composer uses the value of `http_proxy` to proxy https requests, this is not how curl works and I guess others. ``` chris@kinslayer:~ $ http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:3000 curl -sv http://example.com/ > /dev/null * Hostname was NOT found in DNS cache * Trying 127.0.0.1... * connect to 127.0.0.1 port 3000 failed: Connection refused * Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 3000: Connection refused * Closing connection 0 chris@kinslayer:~ $ http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:3000 curl -sv https://example.com/ > /dev/null * Hostname was NOT found in DNS cache * Trying 172.16.58.3... * Connected to example.com (93.184.216.34) port 443 (#0) snip * Connection #0 to host example.com left intact ```

- well, looks like your PHP setup is not able to resolve the DNS
- Auto-closing this as it's marked as support request and has not received any update in a long time.
- FIX: unset no_proxy and NO_PROXY environment variables

Title: PHP cURL not fetching webpage Description: As you can see in the code, I am trying to execute an FQL query and retrieve results. The query I generate is completely fine because I have tested it through my browser. I first used file_get_contents() to retrieve the webpage but it was gicing me a 400 Bad Request Error. Somebody suggest cURL instead. The code segment given below gives me false for $query. If I uncomment the urlencode() line, the script goes on and on and hits the maximum execution time limit. What am I doing wrong? $limit = $start + 100; $query = "select post_id, created_time, actor_id, message, attachment, comments, likes, type from stream where source_id = $id limit $start, ". $limit; $url = "https://graph.facebook.com/fql?q=$query&access_token=$token"; //$url = urlencode($url); echo $url.'
'; $curl_handle=curl_init(); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_URL, $url); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, 2); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_PROXY, "tcp://10.3.3.3:8080"); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_USERAGENT, 'Hi!'); $query = curl_exec($curl_handle); var_dump($query); curl_close($curl_handle); edit: Accessing another URL, file_get_contents gave me this error "failed to open stream: Cannot connect to HTTPS server through proxy". Since this one is also HTTPS, cURL might also be facing the same problem. I thought this might lead to an answer. Answers: - For starters, you reuse your $query variable just before you dump it. Second, use urlencode on your (first) $query variable. (Facebooks $token does not need url encoding) edit (does not fit inside in a comment) I've just tried this myself: '; $curl_handle=curl_init(); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_URL, $url); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, 2); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1); $curlres = curl_exec($curl_handle); var_dump($query); print "\n\n"; var_dump($curlres); curl_close($curl_handle); ?> This works without problems. PM me if you want to try this, and I'll give you the URL. I'm not confortable with releasing this into the wild.. Pherhaps the source is your proxy .. edit Aw what the hell .. go nuts! ;) http://hal.su/on/fbCurlTest.php?token=the%20token&id=the%id&start=0 replace the%20token with your token and replace the%20id with your id.

- Hmm that's right, that's really a micro-optimization. The consequence however seems the same - `400 Bad Request` nearly always boils down to speaking SSL to an unencrypted HTTP server in my experience.
- It's not really a micro optimization, the https connection setup time is quite long and since php streams can't do keepalive we end up opening many connections.
- If you pass in a `https://` URL it will use the value from `http_proxy` according to that line. Good point about the protocol switching, if you get a redirect to a URL that uses a different proxy or should bypass a proxy it will still attempt to use the proxy.

- There is no redirect to https for static files. This one redirects because it's a 404 so it gets handled by symfony which then redirects to force https. If you try a valid url it'll go through over http just fine.

- Because those URLs are based on the file content hash so they change often and old files get cleaned up.
- That fast? So it could very well be that the proxy is caching the `packages.json` a day as it's a static file, serving the client a somewhat outdated version, referencing a sub-include that no longer exists, causing the HTTPS redirect, thus exposing the HTTPS_PROXY mismatch issue on curl internal redirects?
- If the proxy is completely borked and caching what it shouldn't cache, sure it's possible. We clean up files hourly IIRC.
- The response headers on `packages.json` are: ``` Accept-Ranges:bytes Connection:keep-alive Content-Length:1181 Content-Type:application/json Date:Fri, 19 Feb 2016 15:00:38 GMT ETag:"56c72e01-49d" Last-Modified:Fri, 19 Feb 2016 15:00:17 GMT Server:nginx ``` Just an ETag, no `Cache-control` or `Expires`. I wouldn't at all be surprised if this is what's happening if the file starts causing this after an hour. As there is no `must-revalidate` rule or anything these headers tell the proxy it's essentially fine to cache this file for an arbitrary time. I would at the very least configure nginx to add: cache-control: private, max-age=0, no-cache,
- Fair enough, I added no-cache headers on that file now.

- well, looks like your PHP setup is not able to resolve the DNS

Title: PHP cURL not fetching webpage Description: As you can see in the code, I am trying to execute an FQL query and retrieve results. The query I generate is completely fine because I have tested it through my browser. I first used file_get_contents() to retrieve the webpage but it was gicing me a 400 Bad Request Error. Somebody suggest cURL instead. The code segment given below gives me false for $query. If I uncomment the urlencode() line, the script goes on and on and hits the maximum execution time limit. What am I doing wrong? $limit = $start + 100; $query = "select post_id, created_time, actor_id, message, attachment, comments, likes, type from stream where source_id = $id limit $start, ". $limit; $url = "https://graph.facebook.com/fql?q=$query&access_token=$token"; //$url = urlencode($url); echo $url.'
'; $curl_handle=curl_init(); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_URL, $url); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, 2); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_PROXY, "tcp://10.3.3.3:8080"); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_USERAGENT, 'Hi!'); $query = curl_exec($curl_handle); var_dump($query); curl_close($curl_handle); edit: Accessing another URL, file_get_contents gave me this error "failed to open stream: Cannot connect to HTTPS server through proxy". Since this one is also HTTPS, cURL might also be facing the same problem. I thought this might lead to an answer. Answers: - For starters, you reuse your $query variable just before you dump it. Second, use urlencode on your (first) $query variable. (Facebooks $token does not need url encoding) edit (does not fit inside in a comment) I've just tried this myself: '; $curl_handle=curl_init(); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_URL, $url); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, 2); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1); $curlres = curl_exec($curl_handle); var_dump($query); print "\n\n"; var_dump($curlres); curl_close($curl_handle); ?> This works without problems. PM me if you want to try this, and I'll give you the URL. I'm not confortable with releasing this into the wild.. Pherhaps the source is your proxy .. edit Aw what the hell .. go nuts! ;) http://hal.su/on/fbCurlTest.php?token=the%20token&id=the%id&start=0 replace the%20token with your token and replace the%20id with your id.

- Because those URLs are based on the file content hash so they change often and old files get cleaned up.

I wouldn't at all be surprised if this is what's happening if the file starts causing this after an hour. As there is no `must-revalidate` rule or anything these headers tell the proxy it's essentially fine to cache this file for an arbitrary time. I would at the very least configure nginx to add: cache-control: private, max-age=0, no-cache,

Running next line: ``` $ curl -sS https://getcomposer.org/installer| php#!/usr/bin/env php` ``` I'm getting... ``` Some settings on your machine may cause stability issues with Composer. If you encounter issues, try to change the following: Your PHP (5.3.3) is quite old, upgrading to PHP 5.3.4 or higher is recommended. Composer works with 5.3.2+ for most people, but there might be edge case issues. Downloading... Download failed: file_get_contents(https://getcomposer.org/composer.phar): failed to open stream: Cannot connect to HTTPS server through proxy Downloading... Download failed: file_get_contents(https://getcomposer.org/composer.phar): failed to open stream: Cannot connect to HTTPS server through proxy The download failed repeatedly, aborting. ``` But next line is successful ``` $ curl -sS https://getcomposer.org/installer | php -- --disable-tls ```

Comments:
- Well, maybe you also need to set HTTPS_PROXY
- I did that too even is useless. Installer checks only for HTTP_PROXY. See HttpClient::getMergedStreamContext(): ```php // Handle system proxy if (!empty($_SERVER['HTTP_PROXY']) || !empty($_SERVER['http_proxy'])) { // Some systems seem to rely on a lowercased version instead... $proxy = parse_url(!empty($_SERVER['http_proxy']) ? $_SERVER['http_proxy'] : $_SERVER['HTTP_PROXY']); } ```
- hmm, this seems an issue in the installer script, which has not been kept in sync with changes in Composer.
- See, my PHP is old. Couldn't be that?
- The installer uses the HTTP_PROXY value for both http and https.
- @username_2 this is what Composer was doing in the past too, and which was changed to improve things (as some proxies should not be used for HTTPS but only for HTTP). See the comment on https://github.com/composer/getcomposer.org/blob/master/web/installer#L677
- But unless he has a different proxy for http and https, it's not going to make a difference in this scenario :-\

- Hmm that's right, that's really a micro-optimization. The consequence however seems the same - `400 Bad Request` nearly always boils down to speaking SSL to an unencrypted HTTP server in my experience.
- It's not really a micro optimization, the https connection setup time is quite long and since php streams can't do keepalive we end up opening many connections.
- If you pass in a `https://` URL it will use the value from `http_proxy` according to that line. Good point about the protocol switching, if you get a redirect to a URL that uses a different proxy or should bypass a proxy it will still attempt to use the proxy.
- Yes it does but line 49 below overwrites it with the `HTTPS_PROXY` value if set and https url. The underlying issue seems to be indeed that protocol switches do not use the right URL. Bringing us to that the optimization, micro or not, is invalid as http://packagist.org/p/provider-2013%24907f12bc7ed756034fb97405ced3ebfe769ac49a0786554246a14a1b23ffba8e.json instantly redirects with a 307 to the https version right now. So yes, it would appear that the issue is with Composer still trying those URLs as plain http, not setting the `HTTPS_PROXY` for that, and the internal redirect being handled at curl level causing the `http_proxy` to be used for https, explaining the 400 error.
- There is no redirect to https for static files. This one redirects because it's a 404 so it gets handled by symfony which then redirects to force https. If you try a valid url it'll go through over http just fine.
- Errr true, but why is that URL invalid as I copy/pasted it from the error logs? ``` [Composer\Downloader\TransportException] The 'http://packagist.org/p/provider-2013%24907f12bc7ed756034fb97405ced3ebfe769ac49a0786554246a14a1b23ffba8e.json' URL could not be accessed: HTTP/1.0 400 Bad Request ```
- Because those URLs are based on the file content hash so they change often and old files get cleaned up.
- That fast? So it could very well be that the proxy is caching the `packages.json` a day as it's a static file, serving the client a somewhat outdated version, referencing a sub-include that no longer exists, causing the HTTPS redirect, thus exposing the HTTPS_PROXY mismatch issue on curl internal redirects?
- If the proxy is completely borked and caching what it shouldn't cache, sure it's possible. We clean up files hourly IIRC.
- The response headers on `packages.json` are: ``` Accept-Ranges:bytes Connection:keep-alive Content-Length:1181 Content-Type:application/json Date:Fri, 19 Feb 2016 15:00:38 GMT ETag:"56c72e01-49d" Last-Modified:Fri, 19 Feb 2016 15:00:17 GMT Server:nginx ``` Just an ETag, no `Cache-control` or `Expires`. I wouldn't at all be surprised if this is what's happening if the file starts causing this after an hour. As there is no `must-revalidate` rule or anything these headers tell the proxy it's essentially fine to cache this file for an arbitrary time. I would at the very least configure nginx to add: cache-control: private, max-age=0, no-cache,

Title: PHP cURL not fetching webpage Description: As you can see in the code, I am trying to execute an FQL query and retrieve results. The query I generate is completely fine because I have tested it through my browser. I first used file_get_contents() to retrieve the webpage but it was gicing me a 400 Bad Request Error. Somebody suggest cURL instead. The code segment given below gives me false for $query. If I uncomment the urlencode() line, the script goes on and on and hits the maximum execution time limit. What am I doing wrong? $limit = $start + 100; $query = "select post_id, created_time, actor_id, message, attachment, comments, likes, type from stream where source_id = $id limit $start, ". $limit; $url = "https://graph.facebook.com/fql?q=$query&access_token=$token"; //$url = urlencode($url); echo $url.'
'; $curl_handle=curl_init(); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_URL, $url); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, 2); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_PROXY, "tcp://10.3.3.3:8080"); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_USERAGENT, 'Hi!'); $query = curl_exec($curl_handle); var_dump($query); curl_close($curl_handle); edit: Accessing another URL, file_get_contents gave me this error "failed to open stream: Cannot connect to HTTPS server through proxy". Since this one is also HTTPS, cURL might also be facing the same problem. I thought this might lead to an answer. Answers: - For starters, you reuse your $query variable just before you dump it. Second, use urlencode on your (first) $query variable. (Facebooks $token does not need url encoding) edit (does not fit inside in a comment) I've just tried this myself: '; $curl_handle=curl_init(); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_URL, $url); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, 2); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1); $curlres = curl_exec($curl_handle); var_dump($query); print "\n\n"; var_dump($curlres); curl_close($curl_handle); ?> This works without problems. PM me if you want to try this, and I'll give you the URL. I'm not confortable with releasing this into the wild.. Pherhaps the source is your proxy .. edit Aw what the hell .. go nuts! ;) http://hal.su/on/fbCurlTest.php?token=the%20token&id=the%id&start=0 replace the%20token with your token and replace the%20id with your id.

- It's not really a micro optimization, the https connection setup time is quite long and since php streams can't do keepalive we end up opening many connections.
- If you pass in a `https://` URL it will use the value from `http_proxy` according to that line. Good point about the protocol switching, if you get a redirect to a URL that uses a different proxy or should bypass a proxy it will still attempt to use the proxy.

- Because those URLs are based on the file content hash so they change often and old files get cleaned up.
- That fast? So it could very well be that the proxy is caching the `packages.json` a day as it's a static file, serving the client a somewhat outdated version, referencing a sub-include that no longer exists, causing the HTTPS redirect, thus exposing the HTTPS_PROXY mismatch issue on curl internal redirects?
- If the proxy is completely borked and caching what it shouldn't cache, sure it's possible. We clean up files hourly IIRC.
- The response headers on `packages.json` are: ``` Accept-Ranges:bytes Connection:keep-alive Content-Length:1181 Content-Type:application/json Date:Fri, 19 Feb 2016 15:00:38 GMT ETag:"56c72e01-49d" Last-Modified:Fri, 19 Feb 2016 15:00:17 GMT Server:nginx ``` Just an ETag, no `Cache-control` or `Expires`. I wouldn't at all be surprised if this is what's happening if the file starts causing this after an hour. As there is no `must-revalidate` rule or anything these headers tell the proxy it's essentially fine to cache this file for an arbitrary time. I would at the very least configure nginx to add: cache-control: private, max-age=0, no-cache,
- Fair enough, I added no-cache headers on that file now.

Title: PHP cURL not fetching webpage Description: As you can see in the code, I am trying to execute an FQL query and retrieve results. The query I generate is completely fine because I have tested it through my browser. I first used file_get_contents() to retrieve the webpage but it was gicing me a 400 Bad Request Error. Somebody suggest cURL instead. The code segment given below gives me false for $query. If I uncomment the urlencode() line, the script goes on and on and hits the maximum execution time limit. What am I doing wrong? $limit = $start + 100; $query = "select post_id, created_time, actor_id, message, attachment, comments, likes, type from stream where source_id = $id limit $start, ". $limit; $url = "https://graph.facebook.com/fql?q=$query&access_token=$token"; //$url = urlencode($url); echo $url.'
'; $curl_handle=curl_init(); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_URL, $url); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, 2); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_PROXY, "tcp://10.3.3.3:8080"); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_USERAGENT, 'Hi!'); $query = curl_exec($curl_handle); var_dump($query); curl_close($curl_handle); edit: Accessing another URL, file_get_contents gave me this error "failed to open stream: Cannot connect to HTTPS server through proxy". Since this one is also HTTPS, cURL might also be facing the same problem. I thought this might lead to an answer. Answers: - For starters, you reuse your $query variable just before you dump it. Second, use urlencode on your (first) $query variable. (Facebooks $token does not need url encoding) edit (does not fit inside in a comment) I've just tried this myself: '; $curl_handle=curl_init(); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_URL, $url); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, 2); curl_setopt($curl_handle, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1); $curlres = curl_exec($curl_handle); var_dump($query); print "\n\n"; var_dump($curlres); curl_close($curl_handle); ?> This works without problems. PM me if you want to try this, and I'll give you the URL. I'm not confortable with releasing this into the wild.. Pherhaps the source is your proxy .. edit Aw what the hell .. go nuts! ;) http://hal.su/on/fbCurlTest.php?token=the%20token&id=the%id&start=0 replace the%20token with your token and replace the%20id with your id.

提交 Issue 之前请先阅读 [Issue 指引](https://github.com/v2ray/v2ray-core/blob/master/.github/SUPPORT.md)，然后回答下面的问题，谢谢。 除非特殊情况，请完整填写所有问题。不按模板发的 issue 将直接被关闭。 如果你遇到的问题不是 V2Ray 的 bug，比如你不清楚要如何配置，请使用[Discussion](https://github.com/v2ray/discussion/issues)进行讨论。 1) 你正在使用哪个版本的 V2Ray？（如果服务器和客户端使用了不同版本，请注明） 4.18 2) 你的使用场景是什么？比如使用 Chrome 通过 Socks/VMess 代理观看 YouTube 视频。 使用Proxifier轉發v2ray的代理到Steam 3) 你看到的不正常的现象是什么？（请描述具体现象，比如访问超时，TLS 证书错误等） 在連線Steam Community時，在同一個網路環境下，有時可以正常訪問，但是有時顯示：Steam錯誤代碼：-7，但在客戶端不能訪問的同時，通過Chrome連接同一個v2ray代理卻能夠穩定的訪問Steam Community 4) 你期待看到的正确表现是怎样的？ 可以在Steam Client穩定訪問Steam Community 5) 请附上你的配置（提交 Issue 前请隐藏服务器端IP地址）。 服务器端配置: ```javascript { "inbound": { "port": 23854, "listen":"127.0.0.1", "protocol": "vmess", "settings": { "clients": [ { "id": "3de...19", "alterId": 64 } ] }, "streamSettings": { "network": "ws", "wsSettings": { "path": "/gay" } } }, "outbound": { "protocol": "freedom", "settings": {} }, "outboundDetour": [ { "protocol": "blackhole", "settings": {}, "tag": "blocked" } ], "routing": { "strategy": "rules", "settings": { "rules": [ { "type": "field", "ip": [ "0.0.0.0/8", "10.0.0.0/8", "100.64.0.0/10", "127.0.0.0/8", "169.254.0.0/16", "172.16.0.0/12", "192.0.0.0/24", "192.0.2.0/24", "192.168.0.0/16", "198.18.0.0/15", "198.51.100.0/24", "203.0.113.0/24", "::1/128", "fc00::/7", "fe80::/10" ], "outboundTag": "blocked" } ] } } } ``` [Truncated] 8) 其它相关的配置文件（如 Nginx）和相关日志。 Caddyfile: ...(這個和上文的客戶端中的...相同) { log /var/log/caddy.log proxy /gay localhost:23854 { websocket header_upstream -Origin } } 9) 如果 V2Ray 无法启动，请附上 `--test` 输出。 通常的命令为 `/usr/bin/v2ray/v2ray --test --config /etc/v2ray/config.json`。请按实际情况修改。 10) 如果 V2Ray 服务运行不正常，请附上 journal 日志。 通常的命令为 `journalctl -u v2ray`。 v2ray對於其他的網頁來說，可以正常啟動，也運行正常。
